assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with neutral atoms in a magic wavelength trap pushed time and frequency metrology to the 1e-18 level, beyond the caesium definition by orders of magnitude. The original idea (Katori) is a clean, simple and powerful use of laser spectroscopy and light shifts. Its impact reaches redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches. Few developments better embody the measurement-limited view of progress.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated it; Ye drove the record accuracy and stability, and the Sr-lattice clock comparisons. Two laureates is a natural and clean allocation. Other contributors (Lemonde, Gill, Hinkley/Ludlow in other groups, Hall and Hänsch comb background) are not in the credited list and the combs have already been recognised in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced and surpassed each other's accuracy; the field is mature and the practical redefinition of the SI second is approaching but not yet formally adopted. Timing is excellent.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to separate the clock concept from the frequency-comb and ion-clock lineage already honoured (2005, 2012).
Redefinition of the second has not yet happened, which some members might treat as a maturity milestone.
I do not claim to have independently checked the current best uncertainty figures.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal of 1995 turned trapped ions into a concrete architecture for quantum gates, and Blatt's group and others realised gates, entanglement and algorithms with high fidelity. The work forms a pillar of experimental quantum information and is conceptually original, and a direct, reliable route to controllable quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: Theory credit clearly belongs to Cirac and Zoller; experimental realisation is shared between Blatt, Wineland (already honoured in 2012, not credited here), Monroe and Innsbruck/NIST/Oxford groups. Naming Blatt alone from the experimental side could be contested, which weakens the configuration somewhat.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: three decades of independent confirmation, commercial trapped-ion processors, and repeated high-fidelity demonstrations. Recognition is arguably already due.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland) and with the other Cirac/Zoller candidates on the list may complicate allocation.
Experimental credit beyond Blatt (e.g. Monroe, Wineland) is unresolved.
Unclear whether the committee sees it as distinct from the broader quantum-computing recognition in 2025.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single spins in diamond (NV and related centres) opened room-temperature quantum sensing and spin-photon interfaces, from nanoscale magnetometry to biological measurement and quantum networks. The work is experimentally elegant and links directly to the measurement-precision theme and to my own interest in optically addressed solid-state spins and coherence.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko did the foundational single-NV optical detection and coherent control; Awschalom contributed major work on spin coherence in diamond and silicon carbide and in quantum-network directions. Lukin, also in the credited list, is a strong claimant but I leave him out to keep a coherent three-person set, which is a real allocation tension.
assessment.maturity: Single-NV detection dates to 1997 and has been replicated worldwide; applications are broad and growing. Mature for the core discovery, while some network applications are still developing.
uncertainties: The four-name credit list, with Lukin, implies a hard choice.
Whether the prize should reward the detection and control of single spins or the later sensing applications.
Priority and relative credit between Wrachtrup, Jelezko and others on the earliest results is not fully clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 protocol) is a foundational idea in quantum information, using physical principles for secure communication; it has given rise to real-world networks and satellite links. Conceptually original and with lasting influence, though the physical principle rests on earlier foundations of quantum mechanics.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the clear originators of BB84; Ekert's 1991 proposal of entanglement-based key distribution is distinctive and connects to Bell tests. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not in the credited list. A three-person prize is plausible but the Ekert-versus-Bennett-Brassard weighing is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Very mature theoretically and experimentally; many independent implementations. Deployed technology now supports timeliness, and the 2022 entanglement prize makes the connection natural.
uncertainties: Whether a physics prize should honour a protocol whose practical security depends heavily on implementation and engineering.
Weighing the role of Ekert against Bennett and Brassard.
Possible overlap with the 2022 Bell-test prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise controllable many-body Hamiltonians, including the superfluid-Mott insulator transition, and enable quantum simulation with single-site resolution (quantum gas microscopes). It is a major platform in atomic physics with deep links to condensed-matter questions and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, not credited) provided the theoretical proposal for the Hubbard model in lattices; Bloch and Greiner built and extended the experimental platform and microscopes. Cirac also appears in the list, and the four-name credit forces choices; Greiner's role overlaps with the Greiner-Hänsch-Bloch Mott results. Jaksch and Hänsch are absent, so the theory credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across many groups, and applications continue to broaden. Some of the quantum-simulation claims about real advantage over classical methods are still developing.
uncertainties: Theory credit is incomplete without Jaksch, who is not on the list.
Overlap with the Cirac/Zoller candidates and the 2001 BEC and 2012 prizes.
Choice between pioneering platform work and the later quantum-gas-microscope results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs-like boson at the LHC in 2012 was a spectacular experimental feat, confirming the last piece of the Standard Model and validating years of detector and analysis development. Its significance is beyond doubt, although the underlying theory was honoured in 2013.
assessment.attribution: A collaboration of several thousand people; the Nobel statutes are poorly suited. The three credited names are the founding spokespersons or conveners, an imperfect proxy for decisive contribution. Detector concepts, trigger and analysis leaders and the machine builders are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The Higgs couplings are increasingly well measured and the discovery is firmly established. Timing could be seen as late-ish but the allocation problem has stalled recognition.
uncertainties: Attributing a large-collaboration result to three individuals is intrinsically contentious.
Statutes and precedent on collaborations are unresolved.
The theory prize in 2013 may reduce urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Solid-state femtosecond lasers (Ti:sapphire, Kerr-lens mode locking, SESAMs) made ultrashort pulses reliable and compact, underlying ultrafast spectroscopy, frequency combs and attosecond science. The technique is an enabling invention with pervasive scientific use, familiar to me from time-resolved and coherent-optics work.
assessment.attribution: Moulton invented Ti:sapphire as a laser medium, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode locking, and Keller developed SESAM mode locking. Spence and others are plausible additional claimants not on the list. The credit is fairly separable but contested around priority of mode locking.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, widely used for decades. Adjacent recognition came in 2018 (chirped pulse amplification) and 2023 (attosecond), so novelty relative to the previous prizes is a question.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2018 and 2023 laser prizes.
Priority for Kerr-lens mode locking among Sibbett, Spence and colleagues is not entirely clear to me.
Possible perception as engineering rather than discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators and the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells opened an entire field of topological band materials. The concept is original and has had a strong lasting influence, even beyond condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological classification; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental observation, working with Zhang's theoretical prediction for HgTe. Zhang (deceased 2018) and Bernevig and Hughes are not credited, and several others (Moore, Balents, Fu) contributed to the 3D case. Allocation is therefore difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, though some aspects such as clean edge transport are still debated. The subject is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Credit for Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes, Fu and Moore is incomplete.
Quantum anomalous Hall candidates overlap with this field.
I am less able to judge condensed-matter details than atomic-physics topics.
